about.p1: I'm Luis Crisanto. I work on projects that combine interface, REST APIs and databases, and I care about understanding how those pieces connect so a system can grow without breaking.
about.p2: I study Systems Engineering at Universidad César Vallejo. Beyond web development I'm drawn to infrastructure, networking, IoT and computer vision, which is the ground of my thesis project.
about.p3: My next step is solutions architecture and the cloud. I'm currently learning AWS: I don't hold certifications yet and I present it as it is, an area of learning.

summary.retailvision: Real-time foot-traffic analytics: detects people by zone from cameras with YOLOv8 and turns it into indicators, a heat map and reports.
summary.alfapet: Clinical management for a veterinary clinic: patients, appointments, history, inventory and sales, with role-based permissions and an RLS-protected database.

caseUi.ctaText: Tell me what you need and we’ll work out how to solve it.

retailvision.problem: Many stores have no way of knowing how many people come in or how they move inside. Without that data, decisions like where to place a product or a promotion are made by eye.
retailvision.solution: RetailVision Analytics detects and tracks people by zone with YOLOv8 from one or several cameras, and turns video into useful information: live indicators, a heat map, dwell time per zone and exportable reports.
retailvision.why: YOLOv8 and OpenCV can detect and track people on video in real time. FastAPI exposes the data through an API and WebSocket, and React presents it in a dashboard that updates instantly.
how: Video capture from a webcam or RTSP cameras, with several configurable cameras.
Detection and tracking of people by zone with YOLOv8 and OpenCV, in Python.
FastAPI server exposing an API and sending live data over WebSocket, plus an MJPEG stream of the processed video.
React dashboard with Monitor, Analysis, Reports and Video views, Recharts charts and a heat map.
Model evaluation metrics (precision, recall and F1), video upload for analysis and a report exportable to PDF.
retailvision.result: End-to-end working system running locally, with the views and reports described. It is not deployed yet, and measured results will be published later.
retailvision.learned: Integrating computer vision with a real-time API and a web interface: from frame to data, and from data to a decision.

alfapet.tagline: Clinical management for a veterinary clinic.
alfapet.problem: A veterinary clinic needs to manage patients, appointments, clinical history, inventory and sales, with different people accessing different information.
alfapet.solution: An internal web system with clinical and management modules, three roles with different permissions and a database that enforces those rules at the engine level.
alfapet.why: Supabase and PostgreSQL with RLS policies move access control into the database, not just the interface. TypeScript and Zod validate data, and React Router with SSR renders on the server.
how: Frontend in React 19 and TypeScript with React Router (SSR), Vite and Tailwind CSS.
Authentication with Supabase Auth and three roles with distinct permissions.
PostgreSQL with RLS policies, RPC functions and audit triggers.
Data validation with Zod and tests with Vitest and pgTAP.
Dockerfile included and deployment on Vercel.
alfapet.result: System deployed and running at alfapet.vercel.app. Access is for registered users only, so there is no public demo. It was evaluated using the ISO 25010 quality model as a reference framework, which is not a certification.
alfapet.learned: Designing layered security with real permissions in the database, and sustaining a project with tests and auditing.

educore.problem: A school must manage enrollment, attendance, grades and report cards, with different roles working on the same data.
educore.solution: EduCore, a web system with three roles covering enrollment, attendance, grades and report card generation.
educore.why: Native PHP with an MVC structure and PostgreSQL hosted on Supabase, with vanilla JavaScript on the client: a simple base, runnable on XAMPP and not tied to a framework.
how: Backend in native PHP 8 with folders organized as MVC.
Interface with HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript.
Three user roles with enrollment, attendance, grades and report card modules.
educore.result: Working system in a local environment. It is not deployed.
educore.learned: Structuring a backend without a framework, modeling academic data in SQL and separating responsibilities by role.
